- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40), model tends to undercorrect; increase forecast slightly to avoid excessive downward bias.  
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots downward; apply a mild upward bias to counteract lagged mean reversion.  
- In periods of strong mean reversion (sentiment neutral to slightly positive), model overestimates downward trend; reduce forecast slope to align with historical volatility.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is falling, model may overreact; cap upward revisions to avoid overcorrection.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates near-term volatility; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to early forecast days if sentiment is volatile.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, model tends to underestimate true price; apply a 0.3–0.7% upward adjustment to offset pessimism.
